item.title: About CRSCheck.com
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
CRSCheck.com is an independent educational calculator and information website for people researching Canada Express Entry. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

Our approach

We aim to make CRS scoring easier to understand by showing a detailed breakdown and links to official rules. Immigration requirements change. Always confirm calculations and eligibility with IRCC before making decisions.

Privacy

This static version calculates scores in your browser. It does not send entered profile details to a server. If you choose to copy a profile-sharing link, that link includes the profile details you entered; treat it as private.

Important disclaimer

Information is educational and is not legal or immigration advice. Calculator outputs are estimates and may contain errors. IRCC is the final authority.

Calculate my CRS score →

Related tools and guides

CRS score guide · Improve your CRS score · IELTS to CLB · Express Entry overview

Sources and updates

Official references: IRCC CRS calculator · IRCC CRS criteria · 2026 scoring changes

Updated October 2026. Scoring rules are changing on November 3, 2026. Always check official IRCC guidance.

item.title: CRS Changes in 2026
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

Effective date matters

The new Labour Market Integration factor is scheduled for November 3, 2026. Do not treat the new job offer points as available before that date.

Canadian experience versus job offer

Under the announced system, eligible Canadian experience can include existing work-length points plus high-wage occupation points. Qualifying job offers can be worth 50, 70 or 100 points depending on the occupation wage category. IRCC compares the two options and awards the higher result, not their sum.

High-wage occupation classification

IRCC determines eligible high-wage occupations by National Occupational Classification codes and published median wage ratios. An applicant’s own salary alone does not establish eligibility.

No LMIA requirement for qualifying offers

From the effective date, IRCC says an LMIA is no longer required for job offers to qualify for program eligibility or CRS points. Genuine-offer and program-specific requirements remain relevant.

Profile recalculation

IRCC says existing profiles will be recalculated and invitation rounds paused during the transition. Review the latest IRCC announcement before interpreting a changed score.

Official references and next steps

Read the official IRCC guidance and compare your results with IRCC’s calculator. Use our CRS calculator to explore how these factors affect your profile.

Editorial note: Published rules can change. Confirm effective dates, language test validity and individual eligibility directly with IRCC.

item.title: Canadian Work CRS Changes November 2026
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

Work-length points

IRCC lists 0, 35, 46, 56, 63 and 70 points for zero through five or more years with an accompanying spouse; without one, 0, 40, 53, 64, 72 and 80.

High-wage experience points

Starting November 3, 2026, qualifying experience of at least 12 months in eligible occupations can earn 20, 40 or 70 additional points based on the published wage tier. Experience must meet IRCC work rules.

The comparison rule

The Labour Market Integration factor uses the higher of Canadian work experience (length plus qualifying high-wage experience) or a qualifying job offer. The factor has a maximum of 150 points.

Transferability is separate

IRCC states that existing work-length criteria continue to apply to skill-transferability combinations; high-wage occupation points are not substituted into those tables.

Official references and next steps

Read the official IRCC guidance and compare your results with IRCC’s calculator. Use our CRS calculator to explore how these factors affect your profile.

Editorial note: Published rules can change. Confirm effective dates, language test validity and individual eligibility directly with IRCC.

First and second official language

French can be selected as the first official language, or as a second official language. The first-language CRS table is substantially different from the second-language table; use your actual NCLC scores for each ability.

Additional French bonus

NCLC 7 or higher in all four French abilities can add 25 points when English is CLB 4 or lower or no English test was taken, or 50 points when all four English abilities are CLB 5 or higher.

A common error

A high French overall score is not sufficient by itself. IRCC evaluates listening, reading, writing and speaking separately. Use an approved TEF Canada or TCF Canada test and the official conversion tables.

Before November 3, 2026

The March 2025 removal of job-offer CRS points remains applicable until the new announced rules begin. A job offer may still matter for eligibility even when it gives no CRS points.

After the scheduled change

Qualifying high-wage offers may provide 50, 70 or 100 points depending on the eligible NOC wage tier. Job offer points are part of the Labour Market Integration factor rather than a separate bonus added on top of Canadian experience points.

Important limitation

Not every job offer is a high-wage offer. The eligible occupation list, genuineness of the offer and program requirements must be checked separately.

item.title: CRS Points by Age
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

Peak age points

Ages 20 through 29 receive the maximum age points: 110 without an accompanying spouse or 100 with one.

Age 30 through 44

At age 30 the age factor falls to 105 without a spouse or 95 with one. Points then generally decline each year; age 44 receives 6 or 5.

Age 45 and above

From age 45, the age factor awards zero points. Other CRS factors can still contribute to a score.

Which age to enter

IRCC instructs applicants to use age on the invitation date if invited, or their current age when planning a profile.

item.content:encoded:
Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

CRS is a ranking score, not an eligibility decision

Express Entry first requires eligibility under at least one managed immigration program. The Comprehensive Ranking System then ranks eligible profiles. A higher score improves relative ranking but never guarantees an invitation.

The 1,200-point structure

The CRS contains up to 600 core and skill-transferability points and up to 600 additional points. Core factors include age, education, language proficiency and qualifying Canadian work experience. A spouse accompanying you can affect the core allocation and add spouse factors.

What changes in November 2026

IRCC announced a Labour Market Integration factor effective November 3, 2026. It considers eligible Canadian work experience and high-wage job offers, but does not simply add both. Use the appropriate date-specific calculator mode.

How to check a result

Enter the actual score of each language ability, not an overall test band. Use the correct education equivalency and only qualifying work experience. Compare the resulting breakdown against the official IRCC calculator before acting.

Official references and next steps

Read the official IRCC guidance and compare your results with IRCC’s calculator. Use our CRS calculator to explore how these factors affect your profile.

item.title: CRS Skill Transferability Points
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

A 100-point ceiling

The total skill-transferability section is capped at 100 points. Education combinations contribute at most 50, foreign-work combinations at most 50, and trade-certificate combinations can contribute within the overall 100-point ceiling.

Education combinations

Post-secondary education can combine with CLB 7+ language results or Canadian work experience. Higher language scores (CLB 9 across all four abilities) and two or more years of Canadian work can raise combination points.

Foreign experience combinations

One to two years of qualifying foreign experience can produce fewer combination points than three or more years. CLB thresholds and Canadian work-length thresholds change the outcome.

Avoid double-counting

Do not add every row from the official table. Each education and foreign-work subsection has its own cap, and the entire transferability section cannot exceed 100.

Official references and next steps

Read the official IRCC guidance and compare your results with IRCC’s calculator. Use our CRS calculator to explore how these factors affect your profile.

Editorial note: Published rules can change. Confirm effective dates, language test validity and individual eligibility directly with IRCC.

item.content:encoded:
Express Entry manages applications for certain skilled-worker immigration programs. You must meet the criteria of at least one eligible program before a CRS ranking becomes relevant.

The three main programs

  • Federal Skilled Worker Program
  • Canadian Experience Class
  • Federal Skilled Trades Program

Typical process

  1. Check eligibility for an Express Entry program.
  2. Gather valid language results and, where necessary, an educational credential assessment.
  3. Create an Express Entry profile and receive a CRS score.
  4. Wait for an invitation round for which you qualify.
  5. If invited, submit a complete permanent residence application within the applicable deadline.

CRS score versus eligibility

The CRS calculator estimates ranking points. It cannot confirm whether you qualify for a program, whether an occupation is eligible, or whether your documents will be accepted.

Invitations

IRCC holds rounds with changing cut-offs and sometimes category-based requirements. Review official invitation rounds.

item.dc:creator: admin

Reviewed against official IRCC information (October 23, 2026). This independent educational guide explains the scoring rule and its practical implications; it is not immigration advice.

Use the right test

Express Entry accepts IELTS General Training, not IELTS Academic. IRCC evaluates the four skills separately and does not convert the overall band into one CRS level.

CLB 9 thresholds

For IELTS General, CLB 9 requires listening 8.0, reading 7.0, writing 7.0 and speaking 7.0. All four must reach the threshold to qualify for CLB-9-across-all-abilities transferability combinations.

CLB 10 thresholds

For IELTS General, CLB 10 begins at listening 8.5, reading 8.0, writing 7.5 and speaking 7.5.

Why CLB 9 matters

Language points increase at CLB 9 and can also unlock larger education and foreign-work transferability combinations. The exact gain depends on your full profile.

Official references and next steps

Read the official IRCC guidance and compare your results with IRCC’s calculator. Use our CRS calculator to explore how these factors affect your profile.

Identify the weakest scoring factors

Start with an accurate CRS breakdown. Age is generally not controllable, but language performance, eligible education, work experience and some additional factors may change.

Target CLB 9 or 10 strategically

A language retest can increase direct language points and skill-transferability points. Calculate the exact benefit from each ability before investing in another test.

Consider French proficiency

Qualifying NCLC 7 results across four French abilities may unlock additional points. This requires a valid approved test and real preparation, not a simple checkbox.

Assess provincial nomination pathways

An eligible Express Entry-linked provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points. Provincial programs have separate requirements, quotas and selection processes.

Verify education credentials

An Educational Credential Assessment may be required for foreign qualifications. Different Canadian equivalency outcomes can materially change your score.

Canadian education can add points

Eligible Canadian credentials can contribute additional CRS points, depending on the credential and qualifying conditions.

Completing studies in Canada does not automatically make someone eligible for Express Entry or the Canadian Experience Class.

French can affect more than one category

NCLC is assessed separately for listening, reading, writing and speaking. Reaching a target in only one or two abilities is not enough for an all-four threshold.

Category-based Express Entry rounds can have their own eligibility criteria. Extra CRS points do not automatically qualify a candidate for a category-based round.

If you are learning French alongside English, calculate your first and second official-language scores using the actual results you expect to achieve, and verify the order of languages in your profile.

Published October 23, 2026 · Reviewed against publicly available IRCC guidance

Important: This is educational content, not immigration or legal advice. IRCC is the source of truth for eligibility, scores and application rules. Recheck information before submitting an application.

Express Entry is a system that manages applications under certain immigration programs. A CRS score ranks eligible candidates in the pool; it does not by itself establish eligibility. First identify which program you may qualify for, then estimate your ranking score.

In this guide

  1. Start with eligibility, not points
  2. Collect the right inputs
  3. Understand the four scoring groups

  5. Recheck after a life change

Start with eligibility, not points

Express Entry is a system that manages applications under certain immigration programs. A CRS score ranks eligible candidates in the pool; it does not by itself establish eligibility. First identify which program you may qualify for, then estimate your ranking score.

Collect the right inputs

Have your age, marital status, spouse accompanying status, recognized education, valid language results, Canadian skilled work and foreign skilled work details ready. You may also need information about a provincial nomination, Canadian credentials or a qualifying sibling.

Understand the four scoring groups

The CRS combines core human-capital factors, accompanying spouse factors, skill transferability and additional points. Each group has limits, and the overall maximum is 1,200. Your first official language is scored ability by ability.

Check caps and combinations

Skill transferability is capped at 100 points. A strong language score can unlock combinations with education or foreign work experience, but you cannot simply add every possible combination without applying the caps.

Recheck after a life change

A birthday, new test result, new credential, different spouse status or additional qualifying work may change your score. Recalculate with the rule set effective on the relevant date.

A first-language score of at least CLB 9 in all four abilities can improve the transferability combinations for qualifying education and foreign work experience. Improving one ability can have a bigger effect than the direct language-point difference.

Compare each result to the relevant threshold. If three skills are already CLB 9 and one is CLB 8, focus on the remaining skill rather than retaking the test without a targeted plan.

Set a baseline with timed practice. Work on the lowest-scoring task types, review mistakes, then repeat a full practice test to measure whether the intervention helped.

Both are approved English tests

The score scales differ

IELTS uses band scores; PTE Core uses a numerical scale. IRCC maps each test ability to CLB separately. A raw numerical comparison between tests is meaningless.

Compare logistics as well as format

Consider the available test dates, cost, test-center access, preferred question format and turnaround information from each official provider. These vary by location and date.

Compare using CLB, not raw scores

Take your estimated Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking results and convert each to CLB. Then calculate the resulting CRS rather than assuming one test awards more points by default.

Avoid a false guarantee

No test is universally easier. Choose based on your strengths and confirm the current approved-test requirements before booking.

Published October 23, 2026 · Reviewed against publicly available IRCC guidance

Important: This is educational content, not immigration or legal advice. IRCC is the source of truth for eligibility, scores and application rules. Recheck information before submitting an application.

CRS age points can decrease after certain birthdays. The impact depends on the applicable age table and whether you have an accompanying spouse.

In this guide

  1. Your age changed
  2. Your language results expired or changed
  3. Your education details changed
  4. Your spouse information changed
  5. Your work history was reassessed
  6. The rules changed

Your age changed

CRS age points can decrease after certain birthdays. The impact depends on the applicable age table and whether you have an accompanying spouse.

Your language results expired or changed

Approved language results have validity requirements. A different score in just one ability can change both core language points and skill-transferability combinations.

Your education details changed

A credential reassessment, an updated ECA or an incorrect equivalency selection can alter core education points and some transferability combinations.

Your spouse information changed

Accompanying spouse status changes the core-factor table and can introduce spouse education, language and Canadian experience points.

Your work history was reassessed

Qualifying work must meet the applicable immigration requirements. An inaccurate date, occupation classification or duration may change the number of recognized years.

The rules changed

CRS rules can change on specified effective dates. Always compare scores under the rules in force when IRCC evaluates your profile.
